QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_43

question.text: Under SEBI's CSCRF, Managers of AIFs/VCFs classified as Self-Certification REs and with a client base of less than 100 are:

answer.text: Required to use the MII-operated SOC only
EXEMPTED from the mandatory Market-SOC (M-SOC) requirement
Not required to comply with any cyber-security norms
Required to maintain their own full-fledged SOC

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI's CSCRF (workbook pages 250-251), all AIFs must comply with CSCRF by August 31, 2025. Managers of AIFs/VCFs are classified at manager level: Self-Certification REs are those with a corpus of Rs. 3,000 crore and below at the manager level. Where such Self-Certification REs additionally have a client base of less than 100, they are EXEMPTED from the mandatory Market-SOC (M-SOC) requirement. The Trap: Maintaining a full-fledged in-house SOC is not required for this small-RE category. Restricting them to an MII-operated SOC is over-specified — the rule is exemption, not mandatory MII-SOC use. The "no cyber-security norms" option is never correct, since CSCRF compliance itself still applies. Note: The two conditions are cumulative — both the Self-Certification RE classification (manager-level corpus threshold) and the under-100 client base must be satisfied for the M-SOC exemption to apply.
